paper.002: ORVA Protocol is a RWA-DeFi protocol that uses the integrated entity project of natural gas production, transportation, storage and trade in Kaijiang County as the underlying source of cash flow. The total investment in the physical project is about 1 billion yuan, including a daily processing gas gathering station of 1 million cubic meters, a 300 million cubic meter gas storage facility converted from abandoned wells, a 50-kilometer gathering and transportation pipeline, and a natural gas trading business relying on the national pipeline network shipper qualifications. The total construction period of the project is 24 months and will be implemented in two phases. After full production, the annual natural gas turnover will be 300 million cubic meters, generating gathering and transportation service fees, income from seasonal gas storage, and natural gas trading operating cash flow.
paper.003: The entity outputs auditable purchase and sale contracts, IoT measurement data and payment vouchers, which are uploaded to the chain after the oracle completes authenticity verification; the agreement obtains cash income from the entity business through effective service and income arrangements, enters the protocol treasury, and then connects ORVA's long-term participants with open and transparent on-chain rules. Users lock ORVA tokens into the staking contract. The contract records the lock-up quantity, lock-up period and actual participation time. Rewards and governance weights are calculated based on this. The rewards are tilted towards long-term lock-up participants.
paper.004: The protocol integrates complete basic DeFi components: RWA asset registration, staking locking, RWA-Vault, income stream distributor, Gauge weight voting and treasury management contract. The RWA certificate on the chain represents four types of energy rights and interests: gas source income rights, gathering and transportation facility service income rights, gas storage capacity usage rights, and natural gas trade cash flow rights; RWA can be deposited in Vault to obtain the economic rights custody capacity within the DeFi ecosystem. After the entity's cash flow is converted into protocol revenue, it is distributed to lock-up participants according to public rules.
paper.005: ORVA Protocol adheres to the principle of "entity cash flow is the basis, DeFi is an economic rights synergy tool". On the one hand, it solves the practical pain points of the natural gas industry chain such as difficulty in confirming rights, cumbersome reconciliation, and insufficient liquidity of peaking assets. On the other hand, it uses staking locking and revenue flow mechanisms to align the interests of long-term participants. The agreement strictly distinguishes between offline entity operations and on-chain DeFi rights and interests: natural gas physical production, purchase and sale, safety production, hazardous chemicals and pipeline network operations are all executed by off-chain operating businesses in accordance with domestic energy regulatory regulations; the DeFi module is oriented to overseas on-chain ecology, and token issuance, trading and financialization activities are not carried out domestically.
paper.006: Industrial background and core pain points
paper.008: Kaijiang County is located in the natural gas-rich area of northeastern Sichuan. There are a large number of marginal gas wells, low-yield gas wells and abandoned oil and gas wells scattered around it. The daily production capacity of scattered natural gas exceeds 2 million cubic meters. For a long time, regional scattered gas has had problems such as scattered collection, high transportation costs, and low utilization efficiency. CNG tankers are often used for external transportation, resulting in serious waste of resources. There is a lack of large-scale gas storage and peak-shaving facilities in the county and surrounding areas, and the pressure to maintain gas supply during winter peaks is high. Relying on the opportunities of the “15th Five-Year Plan” energy plan, Kaijiang County launched the construction of an integrated natural gas production, transportation, storage and trade project: a new gas gathering station with a daily processing capacity of 1 million cubic meters, a 300 million cubic meter gas storage renovated, and a 50-kilometer gas gathering and transportation pipeline connected to the Jinshan valve chamber of the national pipeline network to send gas from Sichuan to the east. At the same time, relying on the national pipeline network shipper qualifications to carry out "upstream procurement-pipeline network consignment-downstream sales" integrated trade, realizing the entire chain of production, transmission, storage, and trade.
paper.009: Pain points of traditional industry chain
paper.010: It is difficult to confirm the ownership of scattered gas assets: scattered gas wells are scattered, production capacity and income are recorded in offline ledgers, assets are difficult to evaluate in a standardized manner, and financing channels for heavy asset projects are limited.
paper.011: Multi-party settlement and reconciliation are cumbersome: upstream gas sources, gathering and transportation operators, gas storage and peaking parties, and trading sellers rely on offline reconciliation, with long settlement cycles and high risks of manual errors.
paper.012: The value of gas storage capacity cannot be flexibly transferred: the 300 million cubic meter gas storage has peak shaving value of "summer injection and winter mining", but under the traditional model, the storage usage rights are difficult to split and transfer, and the peak shaving resource allocation efficiency is low.
paper.013: Operational data islands: wellhead collection, gas gathering station processing, gas storage injection and production, and pipeline network metering data are scattered in different business systems, making cross-organization verification difficult.
paper.014: Insufficient sharing of peak shaving risks: There is great pressure to ensure gas supply during winter peaks, and there is a lack of market-based tools to allow all parties in the industry to share peak shaving costs and benefits.
paper.015: The gap between traditional RWA and DeFi
paper.016: Existing RWA practices mostly focus on static asset deposits and lack standardized DeFi tools that match the entity's operating cash flow: assets can only be "certified" and difficult to "participate", and there is a lack of staking locking, automatic distribution of income streams, and long-term participant incentive mechanisms; the interests of participants cannot be deeply bound to the long-term operating cycle of the project, and short-term speculation can easily interfere with industry goals.
paper.018: Offline entities generate real contracts, measurement and payment collection, and the oracle PoR reserve certification mechanism completes on-chain verification;
paper.019: RWA puts four types of energy rights and interests on the chain and stores them as certificates. The certificates only represent economic rights and interests and do not represent physical property rights;
paper.020: Introducing DeFi staking staking: users lock ORVA, and calculate rewards and governance weights based on the three-dimensional factor of "locked amount + locking period + actual participation time";
paper.021: The entity business output agreement service income is distributed to the lock-up participants through the income flow contract according to public rules;
paper.022: Set up the RWA-Vault vault and Gauge voting components, the industry committee controls the bottom line of entity compliance, and the DAO is responsible for protocol parameters and treasury governance.
paper.025: Build a RWA-DeFi infrastructure driven by real energy operating cash flow, digitize the rights and interests of the county natural gas production-transmission-storage-trade industry chain in a credible way, align the interests of long-term participants through DeFi staking locking and revenue flow mechanisms, and provide a reusable agreement template for global entity energy RWA.
paper.027: Anchoring the real operating activities of the Kaijiang natural gas entity project, DeFi is used as an on-chain tool to empower entities, without replacing or interfering with offline energy production and operations; it solves the pain points of energy asset confirmation, reconciliation, and liquidity; it clearly demarcates the boundaries between physical business and DeFi economic rights on the chain.
paper.029: Source of underlying cash flow: operating cash collection from Kaijiang County natural gas production, transportation, storage and trade integration project;
paper.030: RWA layer: deposit of four types of energy economic rights certificates;
paper.031: DeFi layer: ORVA staking lock-up contract, RWA-Vault vault, income stream distribution, Gauge voting, treasury management;
paper.032: Participation rules: ORVA lock-up participation, the weight is calculated by the lock-up quantity, lock-up period and actual participation time;
paper.033: Boundary: Only agreement rights and interests are processed on the chain, and physical delivery of natural gas, safe production, and qualification operations are all completed by off-chain operating businesses.
paper.034: Real industry base: Kaijiang County natural gas production-transmission-storage-trade integration project
paper.035: All RWA assets and ORVA-DeFi protocol income are anchored to the following entity production capacity and operating activities.
paper.036: Gas gathering station project: A new gas gathering station with a daily processing capacity of 1 million cubic meters of natural gas (annual processing capacity of 300 million cubic meters) will be built, equipped with facilities such as pretreatment, compression, metering, and safety monitoring, to achieve unified collection, purification, processing, and efficient gathering and transportation of scattered gas in Kaijiang and surrounding areas.
paper.037: Gas storage and gas transmission pipeline project: A 300-million-cubic-meter gas storage was rebuilt using abandoned oil and gas wells in Kaijiang County, and a 50-kilometer gathering and transportation pipeline was newly built to the Jinshan Valve Chamber of the Sichuan-East Gas Pipeline Network in the national pipeline network to achieve seasonal peak shaving, emergency supply guarantee and resource reserve of "gas injection in summer and gas production in winter".
paper.038: Natural gas trading business: Relying on the qualifications of the national pipeline network shipper, it adopts the integrated model of "upstream procurement-pipeline network consignment-downstream sales", covering industrial users in Kaijiang Economic and Technological Development Zone, industrial and commercial users around Dazhou, and gas consuming enterprises in Wandakai area.
paper.039: Investment and cycle: The total investment of the project is about 1 billion yuan (about 100 million yuan for the gas gathering station, about 500 million yuan for the gas storage and pipeline, and about 400 million yuan for trade operating funds); the total construction period is 24 months, implemented in two phases: the first phase takes 12 months to complete the main construction and qualification of the gas gathering station, and the second phase takes 12 months to complete the transformation of the gas storage, the laying of 50 kilometers of gathering and transportation pipelines, and the joint debugging of the entire system and put into full production.
paper.040: Offline qualification basis: national pipeline network shipper qualification, gas operation license, hazardous chemicals operation license, which are handled by the entity enterprise and operated in compliance with regulations.
paper.041: Complete business closed loop: entity cash flow → RWA asset layer → DeFi protocol layer
paper.043: Gas is produced from scattered gas wells → purified and compressed by gas gathering stations → part of the gas is directly sold through the pipeline network trade, and part is injected into the gas storage; in winter, gas storage peaks are extracted to ensure supply → sold to downstream industries and urban gas users, forming formal commercial contracts, measurement reports and bank receivables.
paper.045: IoT collects measurement data from wellheads, gas gathering stations, and gas storage, and third-party audited payment vouchers. After being verified by the oracle PoR, four types of RWA economic rights vouchers are cast (gas source revenue rights, gathering and transportation facility revenue rights, gas storage capacity usage rights, and trade cash flow rights). RWA only represents a certificate of economic rights and interests, not a physical right to natural gas.
paper.047: The entity project pays the cash income of the agreement service to the ORVA agreement in accordance with the offline service agreement (in the form of a compliant stable currency and collects it on the chain to the protocol treasury); the user submits the ORVA token to the staking lock-up contract and independently selects the lock-up period. The contract records three core variables: lock-up quantity, lock-up period and actual participation time; the contract calculates the reward weight and governance voting weight of the account based on three-dimensional factors. The longer the lock-up time and the longer the actual participation, the greater the weight. The higher the coefficient; after the protocol treasury receives the income from the entity source, the income stream distributor automatically distributes rewards according to the weighted proportion of each account; RWA assets can be deposited into the RWA-Vault vault to implement economic rights certificate custody and Gauge voting configuration; DAO completes voting on protocol governance proposals based on the weighted weight of the lock-up, and the industry committee conducts a pre-compliance review of the proposal; upon expiration of the lock-up, ORVA can be unlocked and retrieved, and a penalty mechanism can be set up for early unlocking to curb short-term speculation.
paper.048: Key boundaries: The natural gas physical sales and production operations of the physical business are completely isolated from DeFi; DeFi only handles service income, token pledges and RWA economic rights certificates at the protocol level.
paper.050: ORVA Protocol adopts a layered architecture: entity perception layer → trusted oracle middleware layer → blockchain bottom layer → ORVA-DeFi core contract layer → API/SDK interface layer → DApp application layer. The original business plaintext data is kept off-chain, and only hashes and key measurement indicators are stored on the chain.
paper.052: IoT measuring instruments at wellheads, gas gathering stations, and gas storage gates collect gas production, processing, gas injection, and gas extraction volumes; physical project ERP, trade contracts, and payment ledgers output business documents; third-party testing and safety verification reports are archived locally, and file hashes are uploaded to the chain.
paper.054: Multi-node oracle cluster: perform multi-source cross-checking on on-site measurement data, reject abnormal data on the chain, and prevent single device data tampering;
paper.055: Institutional KYC access: Enterprise entities participating in RWA business complete identity verification;
paper.056: Privacy processing: Original processes, commercial quotations and sensitive business data are not uploaded to the chain in clear text, only hashes and statistical measurement indicators are uploaded to the chain.
paper.058: Mainnet: used to deploy the full set of ORVA-DeFi contracts;
paper.059: Alliance chain: Provides evidence storage and audit inquiries for domestic entities and regulators;
paper.060: Cross-chain gateway: realizes cross-chain mapping of RWA economic rights certificates after compliance review;
paper.061: Storage strategy: Original business documents and reports are stored in distributed storage, and hash indexes are stored on the chain.
paper.063: RWA asset registration contract: The minting, ownership change and destruction of four types of energy RWA, and issuance must be verified by the oracle and approved by the industry committee;
paper.064: ORVA staking lock-up contract (core module): The user inputs ORVA and selects the lock-up period, and persistently records the lock-up quantity, lock-up period and actual participation timestamp, and dynamically calculates the weighted weight; supports partial unlocking and expiration unlocking; early unlocking triggers the penalty mechanism, and the penalty part goes into the protocol treasury;
paper.065: RWA-Vault vault contract: manages RWA economic rights certificates, supports deposit/withdrawal, and provides asset access for Gauge voting;
paper.066: Income stream distributor contract: reads the treasury income and automatically distributes rewards in a streaming manner according to the weighted weight output by the staking contract;
paper.067: Gauge voting contract: Based on the lock-up weight, voting configures the incentive weights of different RWA pools;
paper.068: protocol treasury contract: collects service income from entity sources, handling fees and early unlocking and confiscation funds, and expenditures must be double-reviewed by DAO voting and the Industry Committee;
paper.069: DAO governance contract and dispute evidence storage contract.
paper.070: API/SDK interface layer and DApp application layer
paper.071: External output interface: entity system docking, regulatory audit inquiry, and third-party DApp development. The DApp side provides entity partner portal (RWA economic rights view), ORVA-DeFi portal (staking locking, weight query, reward collection, Gauge voting, Vault asset management) and audit supervision portal (PoR report hash verification, on-chain income flow query).
paper.073: All smart contracts undergo multiple rounds of third-party security audits and a bug bounty program is established;
paper.074: The oracle machine uses multi-node cross-checking to avoid single-point data falsification;
paper.075: DeFi contracts are physically isolated from the physical production control system, and on-chain contracts cannot control offline equipment at all;
paper.076: The chain only provides economic rights certificates and does not control or interfere with the operation of offline physical equipment and physical natural gas delivery. Safety production is the responsibility of the physical enterprise.
paper.078: Each RWA issuance must meet the following requirements at the same time: complete offline business contract + IoT measurement data verified by the oracle + industry committee approval and confirmation. RWA adopts the ERC-1155 multi-asset standard and only represents economic economic rights certificates and does not represent physical natural gas property rights.
paper.080: Casting conditions: complete offline business contract + IoT measurement data oracle verification + industry committee confirmation, all are indispensable;
paper.081: Transfer restrictions: only open to industry participants who have completed institutional KYC;
paper.082: Destruction conditions: Corresponding to the end of the revenue cycle, the end of the storage capacity use cycle, or the termination of offline rights and interests;
paper.083: Proof of Reserves (PoR): Regularly conduct third-party audits of physical project production capacity, gas storage inventory, and trade ledgers, and the audit report hash is published on the chain.
paper.085: RWA certificates can be deposited into the ORVA-Vault vault to participate in DeFi Gauge incentive voting; RWA itself does not directly generate unsecured loans, but only serves as economic rights custody certificates to avoid the transmission of financial leverage on the chain to physical energy assets.
paper.086: Token Economy and DeFi Core Mechanism
paper.088: ORVA is the protocol's native governance-staking-incentive token: used for protocol staking, reward collection and governance. ORVA is not an entity project equity and does not represent physical natural gas assets; all physical natural gas transactions are settled in legal currency; ORVA-DeFi is oriented to overseas on-chain ecology and does not carry out token financial activities domestically.
paper.090: The total amount of ORVA tokens is fixed and will never be issued additionally. The distribution plan is as follows:
paper.091: Core DeFi staking and weight calculation rules
paper.092: The user calls the staking contract, passes in the ORVA and manually selects the lock-up period (such as 3/6/12 months); the contract permanently saves three key parameters: the amount of ORVA locked (amount), the user-selected lock-in period (lock_term), and the actual continuous participation time of the staking (active_time). Account weight calculation formula:
paper.094: Boost amplification coefficient: The longer the lock-up period and the longer the actual participation duration, the higher the Boost coefficient, which encourages long-term lock-up and inhibits short-term speculation;
paper.095: Early unlocking: Unexpired active unlocking will deduct a certain percentage of ORVA and transfer it to the protocol treasury; there will be no penalty for expired unlocking;
paper.096: For each round of income distribution and each DAO vote, the weighted weight of the staking contract output is read as the basis for distribution and voting.
paper.098: The entity project pays the service income to the ORVA protocol according to the offline service agreement, and enters the on-chain treasury contract in the form of a compliant stable currency. The PoR audit report hash is synchronized on the chain, proving that the income comes from the entity's energy operation receivables;
paper.099: Trigger the income stream distributor contract and read the weighted weight ratio of all staking accounts;
paper.100: Participants can claim rewards with one click on the DApp, and support setting up automatic re-investment;
paper.101: National treasury fund expenditures are divided into DeFi reward distribution, contract security audits and system iterations. Large expenditures must be approved by DAO voting and the industry committee.
paper.103: The RWA-Vault vault is only used for RWA economic rights certificate custody and is not open to high-risk unsecured lending;
paper.104: The Gauge voting module votes based on ORVA weighted by lock-up and allocates different RWA pool incentive resources;
paper.105: The protocol does not issue any stablecoins anchored to natural gas; DeFi tools only serve the economic rights level of the protocol.
paper.106: Governance mechanism: Industry Committee + ORVA-DAO collaborative governance
paper.107: Hard boundaries: Physical engineering construction, gas storage injection and production operations, physical natural gas sales and pricing, production safety and offline commercial contract signing are all executed by offline entity companies in accordance with company laws and energy regulatory regulations; DeFi-DAO has no right to interfere with entity production and operations. Governance is divided into two layers: Industry Committee (pre-compliance review) and ORVA-DAO (on-chain governance based on DeFi staking weighting).
paper.109: Members: entity project representatives, energy industry experts, legal compliance experts. Responsibilities:
paper.110: Review all RWA asset issuance applications and verify the consistency of on-chain economic rights and offline contracts;
paper.111: DAO proposals are subject to pre-compliance review, and proposals that violate energy regulation and entity business security are directly rejected;
paper.112: Select trusted oracle nodes and third-party PoR audit institutions;
paper.113: Secondary confirmation of large-scale expenditure proposals from the treasury.
paper.115: Participation threshold: staking to lock ORVA and obtain weighted voting weight (locked amount + locking period + actual participation time);
paper.116: The voting weight completely reads the weighted value of the staking contract output, preventing pure token capital from completely dominating the industrial agreement;
paper.117: Governance scope: DeFi contract parameter adjustment, Gauge incentive weight configuration, treasury budget proposal, ecosystem incentive rules, oracle node replacement;

paper.164: ORVA Protocol uses the Kaijiang County natural gas production, transportation, storage and trade integrated physical project as a solid industrial base to build a RWA-DeFi protocol driven by real energy cash flow. The protocol relies on the verifiable contract, measurement and repayment data on the entity side to complete the listing of RWA rights and interests on the chain; through the ORVA staking lock-up contract, it records the user's lock-up quantity, lock-up period and actual participation time, and calculates rewards and governance weights accordingly; it integrates a full set of DeFi components such as Vault, revenue stream distribution, and Gauge voting, and the protocol service income comes from the entity's operating cash flow.
